source.title: Abrupt and spontaneous strategy switches emerge in simple regularised neural networks
source.authors: Anika T. Löwe; Léo Touzo; Paul S. Muhle-Karbe; Andrew M. Saxe; C. Summerfield; Nicolas W. Schuck

record.tranche_reason: The paper cites Grokking as an example of delayed or stage-like learning, but its own experiments study insight-like strategy switches in a different task, not delayed generalization on algorithmic datasets.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own results on delayed strategy switching, which are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version. Its task has a hidden change in which feature predicts the correct response; the reported performance is not train/test generalization after overfitting. It does not test dataset-size effects, the proposed grokking mechanisms, realistic pretraining, or optimizer/numerical artifact claims.
record.test_reason: The paper cites the Grokking paper [31] once, as prior work showing insight-like learning can arise from gradient descent. Its own experiments study a sudden strategy switch after an unannounced change in which input feature predicts the answer, in a 2-input gated network trained online. There is no train/test split, no overfitting phase, no algorithmic dataset and no generalization measure, so its results do not bear on any grokking version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that insight-like behaviour (sudden, selective, delayed) can arise from gradual learning in simple networks, through L1-regularised gating, gradient noise and silent weights. They make no claim about grokking or delayed generalization.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a small gated network trained online on a perceptual decision and strategy-switch task, rather than the original algorithmic-dataset generalization setup.
record.method_sensitivity: In the strategy-switch task, the reported effect depends on L1 regularisation and gradient-update noise; its frequency and delay vary with λ.

fits_no_version.finding: In a hidden-regularity strategy-switch task, about 46.5% of L1-gated networks trained with noisy online SGD switch suddenly to the newly predictive feature after a variable delay (mean 175 trials). Switch frequency rises with gradient noise and falls with λ. Delay grows with λ. L2 and unregularised networks lack the selectivity and delay. Pre-set colour weights raise the switch rate to 70.7%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gated networks with L1 regularisation and gradient noise show sudden, selective, delayed strategy switches when an unannounced feature becomes predictive, driven by 'silent' weights under suppressed gates.

record.problems: The study does not evaluate algorithmic generalization or train/test accuracy, and its task introduces a change in feature predictiveness rather than testing grokking. Some mechanism-sweep outcomes are described qualitatively, with numerical values not stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Human behavioral results were left out because the claim concerns networks. Other human results and network mechanism measurements (including individual gradients, gates, and weights) were not included because they characterize the separate insight-like strategy-switch phenomenon rather than grokking or generalization.

untested.parts: No algorithmic dataset, no train-versus-test accuracy gap, no dataset-size sweep.
Silent colour weights under suppressed gates precede the switch, but this is a task-switch mechanism, not a generalizing circuit replacing memorization.
No delayed generalization on non-algorithmic data. No initialization-scale or weight-norm lazy-to-rich manipulation; the weight edit (r6) targets strategy-switch frequency.
L1 and L2 gate regularisation affect switch frequency and delay. There is no circuit-efficiency comparison, critical dataset size or ungrokking.
No comparison of algorithms across runs.
Gradient noise is varied (r5), but not adaptive-optimizer or floating-point artifacts, and not for grokking delays.

record.verdict_notes: Rows are correctly linked to none, and their states (cannot_determine) are appropriate because none measures generalization. r4 is from the hidden-layer network (18/99 insight networks, per Fig. 3E). The single citation of the Grokking paper does not make this a grokking test.

versions.untested_parts: No algorithmic dataset, training-versus-test accuracy comparison, or dataset-size sweep.
The paper studies gated weights and gradients in a strategy-switch task, not a generalizing circuit or continuous measures anticipating a grokking generalization jump.
The task is not a test of grokking-like delayed generalization on non-algorithmic data or of a lazy-to-rich transition controlled by initialization scale or weight norm.
Regularisation is studied for insight-like strategy switches, not for the efficiency of generalizing circuits, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
No test of whether runs converge to the same identifiable algorithm.
The paper investigates gradient noise as a contributor to strategy switching; it does not test adaptive-optimizer or floating-point artifacts in grokking.

rows.subject: L1-regularised neural networks
rows.operation_detail: Classified low-coherence performance changes as insight-like when fitted switch steepness exceeded the control distribution's 100th percentile.

conditions.value: Spontaneous Strategy Switch Task; colour becomes predictive in motion and colour phase

rows.measure: Networks classified as having sudden insight-like performance switches
rows.baseline: Control-network steepness distribution; cutoff was its 100th percentile
rows.locator: Results, Behaviour of L1-regularised Neural Networks; Fig. 3
rows.note: This is a strategy-switch outcome, not a measure of grokking or test generalization.

rows.subject: L1-regularised neural networks
rows.operation_detail: Compared low-coherence accuracy in the halved task blocks before and after individually fitted switch points.
rows.locator: Results, Insight-like Behavioural Characteristics of Network Behaviour; Fig. 3C
rows.note: The measure shows a task-performance switch but cannot establish delayed generalization after overfitting.

rows.subject: L1-regularised neural networks
rows.operation_detail: Measured fitted switch-point delays after colour became predictive.
rows.baseline: Onset of motion and colour phase
rows.value: Average 175 trials (±105 trials); range 2 to 8 trial bins
rows.uncertainty: Exact two-sided Kolmogorov-Smirnov test: D(46) = 0.13, p = 0.85
rows.locator: Results, Insight-like Behavioural Characteristics of Network Behaviour; Fig. 3H
rows.note: Delay is to a strategy switch in this task, not to a test-accuracy rise after overfitting.

rows.subject: L1-regularised neural networks with a hidden layer
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated the proportion showing abrupt and delayed strategy-switch dynamics.
rows.measure: Networks exhibiting abrupt and delayed insight-like learning dynamics
rows.locator: Results, Spontaneous Strategy Switches in Deep Neural Networks; Fig. S1
rows.note: The reported outcome concerns strategy switching, not generalization.

rows.subject: L1-regularised neural networks
rows.operation_detail: Varied the standard deviation of noise added during gradient updates.

conditions.value: No noise versus σξg larger than approximately 0.05

rows.baseline: No gradient-update noise: no insight networks
rows.value: 100% insight networks when σξg reached values larger than approximately 0.05
rows.uncertainty: Error bars are SD; 10 simulations of 99 networks each
rows.locator: Results, Networks Need Noise For Insight-like Behaviour; Fig. 5A
rows.note: This varies gradient noise for the paper's strategy-switch behavior, not for grokking.

rows.subject: L1-regularised neural networks
rows.operation_detail: Adjusted colour and motion weights to the mean absolute sizes observed in insight networks at the start of the motion and colour phase; gates were unchanged.

conditions.value: Weights adjusted before the motion and colour phase

rows.measure: Networks classified as showing insight-like switches
rows.locator: Results, Silent Colour Knowledge Precedes Insight-like Behaviour
rows.note: The weight edit changes the frequency of strategy switches; it is not a test of a grokking initialization-scale or weight-norm account.

rows.subject: L1-regularised neural networks
rows.operation_detail: Varied the L1 regularisation parameter λ.
rows.value: The number linearly decreased with increasing λ
rows.uncertainty: Figure reports error bars as SD; numerical values not stated
rows.locator: Results, Regularisation Parameter λ Affects Insight Behaviour Delay and Frequency; Fig. 5C
rows.note: Qualitative result for strategy-switch frequency, not for a grokking efficiency account.

rows.subject: L1-regularised neural networks
rows.operation_detail: Varied the L1 regularisation parameter λ.
rows.measure: Average switch point in the task
rows.value: The average switch point occurred later with increasing λ
rows.uncertainty: Figure reports error bars as SEM; numerical values not stated
rows.locator: Results, Regularisation Parameter λ Affects Insight Behaviour Delay and Frequency; Fig. 5D
rows.note: This is a delay in the strategy-switch task, not delayed test generalization.

rows.subject: L2-regularised and non-regularised neural networks
rows.operation_detail: Compared the presence of insight-like selectivity and delay with L1-regularised networks.
rows.measure: Selectivity and variable delay of insight-like strategy switches
rows.value: Neither L2-regularised nor non-regularised networks showed the key characteristics of selectivity and delay
rows.locator: Results, Behaviour of L1-regularised Neural Networks; Discussion
rows.note: The paper says L2 networks also showed abrupt performance increases, but lacked the reported selectivity and delay.
